environment.frontend: Your frontend/ code on the Vite dev server, http://localhost:5173
environment.database: An in-memory test database standing in for MongoDB Atlas (same queries; Atlas was not reachable from the test machine)
environment.sample_data: John Doe (SAVINGS $1,500 + CHECKING $0), Ann Lee (no accounts), Joan Smith (SAVINGS $200)

test_cases.expected: "Welcome to Simple Bank", two cards (Customers, Search), the "Simple Bank" header, and a footer with the year
test_cases.actual: Heading "Welcome to Simple Bank"; cards ['Customers', 'Search']; header "Simple Bank"; footer "© 2026 Simple Bank · React + FastAPI + MongoDB Atlas"

test_cases.steps: Click Home, Customers, Search in the header
test_cases.expected: The page changes without a full reload; the current link is highlighted
test_cases.actual: Customers -> /customers (highlighted: Customers); Search -> /search (highlighted: Search); Home -> / (highlighted: Home); full page reload: no

test_cases.steps: On the Welcome page, click the Customers card
test_cases.expected: The Customers page opens
test_cases.actual: Opened /customers with heading "Customers"

test_cases.expected: "Page not found." with the header and footer still showing
test_cases.actual: "Page not found." shown: True; header shown: True; footer shown: True

test_cases.expected: The header wraps, tables scroll sideways, nothing is cut off
test_cases.actual: Page width 375px in a 375px screen (no sideways page scroll: True); table overflow-x: auto; header height 91px (wrapped onto 2 rows)

test_cases.expected: Table lists John Doe, Ann Lee, Joan Smith (plus any older test data); the count matches the rows
test_cases.actual: Rows: ['John Doe', 'Ann Lee', 'Joan Smith']; count "3 total"

test_cases.steps: Network tab: set throttling to "3G", reload Customers
test_cases.expected: "Loading customers..." with a spinner, then the table
test_cases.actual: With 1.5 s network delay: "Loading customers..." and spinner shown: True; then the table appeared with 3 rows
test_cases.note: Slow network simulated with Chrome DevTools throttling (1.5 s latency) instead of the "3G" preset.

test_cases.expected: Red "Cannot reach the server. Is the backend running on port 8000?" with a Retry button
test_cases.actual: Red message "Cannot reach the server. Is the backend running on port 8000?"; Retry button shown: True
test_cases.note: Backend stopped by ending its process (same as Ctrl+C).

test_cases.steps: Start the backend again, click Retry
test_cases.expected: The message disappears and the table loads
test_cases.actual: Error gone: True; table loaded with ['John Doe', 'Ann Lee', 'Joan Smith']
test_cases.note: The test database starts empty after a restart, so the sample data was re-created before clicking Retry.

test_cases.steps: Name "Mia Wong", Email "mia@example.com", click Add customer
test_cases.expected: Green "Added Mia Wong (ID n)."; a new row at the bottom; the count goes up by 1; the inputs clear
test_cases.actual: Notice "Added Mia Wong (ID 4)."; last row "Mia Wong"; rows 3 -> 4 ("4 total"); inputs cleared: True; POST status 200

test_cases.steps: Leave both empty, click Add customer
test_cases.expected: "Name and email are required."; no request in the Network tab
test_cases.actual: Message "Name and email are required."; POST requests sent: 0

test_cases.steps: Name and Email of only spaces, click Add customer
test_cases.expected: The same message (spaces are trimmed)
test_cases.actual: Message "Name and email are required."; POST requests sent: 0

test_cases.expected: The browser blocks it with its own email warning
test_cases.actual: Browser marked the email invalid: True ("Please include an '@' in the email address. 'abc' is missing an '@'."); POST requests sent: 0

test_cases.expected: Mia Wong is still listed (and visible in Atlas)
test_cases.actual: After reload, Mia Wong listed: True; present in the database (GET /api/customers): True
test_cases.note: Atlas check replaced by GET /api/customers on the test database.

test_cases.steps: Click Delete on Mia Wong, then Cancel
test_cases.expected: Nothing changes; no DELETE request
test_cases.actual: Confirm box said "Delete Mia Wong and all their accounts?"; clicked Cancel; rows unchanged: True; DELETE requests: 0

test_cases.steps: Click Delete on Mia Wong, then OK
test_cases.expected: Green "Deleted Mia Wong."; the row is gone; the count goes down by 1
test_cases.actual: Notice "Deleted Mia Wong."; Mia Wong still listed: False; rows 4 -> 3; DELETE status 204

test_cases.expected: Heading "John Doe", ID and email, and an accounts table: SAVINGS $1,500.00 and CHECKING $0.00
test_cases.actual: Heading "John Doe"; details ['ID: 1', 'Email: john@example.com']; account rows ['1 SAVINGS $1,500.00', '2 CHECKING $0.00']

test_cases.expected: "This customer has no accounts yet."
test_cases.actual: Shown: "This customer has no accounts yet."

test_cases.expected: Red "Customer not found" with Retry
test_cases.actual: Red message "Customer not found"; Retry shown: True

test_cases.expected: Red message from the API: "Input should be a valid integer..."
test_cases.actual: Red message "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer"

test_cases.expected: Returns to the customer list
test_cases.actual: Went to /customers

test_cases.actual: Heading "Name starts with "jo""; results ['Joan Smith', 'John Doe']

test_cases.expected: The same two customers
test_cases.actual: Results ['Joan Smith', 'John Doe']

test_cases.expected: "No customers match." (the search matches the start of the name)
test_cases.actual: Shown: "No customers match."

test_cases.expected: "No customers match."
test_cases.actual: Shown: "No customers match."

test_cases.expected: Nothing happens; no request
test_cases.actual: Search requests sent: 0; screen unchanged (still "No customers match.")

test_cases.expected: "No customers match." and no error (the backend escapes it)
test_cases.actual: Shown: "No customers match."; error shown: False; API status 200

test_cases.expected: Only View links, no Delete buttons
test_cases.actual: Delete buttons in results: 0; View links: 2

test_cases.actual: Heading "Customers with an account of $1000 or more"; results ['John Doe']

test_cases.actual: Heading "Customers with an account of $1500 or more"; results ['John Doe']

test_cases.actual: Shown: "No customers match."

test_cases.expected: The browser refuses it (minimum is 0); no request is sent
test_cases.actual: Browser marked -5 invalid: True ("Value must be greater than or equal to 0."); requests sent: 0

test_cases.steps: Stop the backend, run a search
test_cases.expected: Red "Cannot reach the server..."; earlier results are cleared
test_cases.actual: Before: 2 results; after stopping the backend: red "Cannot reach the server. Is the backend running on port 8000?"; result tables on screen: 0
test_cases.note: Backend restarted and sample data re-created afterwards.

test_cases.steps: Network tab, reload Customers, click the `customers` request
test_cases.expected: `GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/customers`, status 200; Preview shows the JSON list
test_cases.actual: GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/customers -> 200; JSON list of 3 customers, first: {"name": "John Doe", "email": "john@example.com", "id": 1}

test_cases.expected: Response header `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173`
test_cases.actual: access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5173

test_cases.steps: Add a customer and watch the Network tab
test_cases.expected: An `OPTIONS` request, then `POST /api/customers` with status 200
test_cases.actual: Backend log: ['OPTIONS /api/customers HTTP/1.1 -> 200 OK', 'POST /api/customers HTTP/1.1 -> 200 OK']; browser saw POST status 200
test_cases.note: Chrome hides preflight requests from automation, so the OPTIONS request was read from the backend's access log. Run in a fresh browser window because Chrome caches a preflight for 10 minutes (CORSMiddleware max_age=600).

test_cases.steps: Add a customer in Swagger, then refresh the React Customers page
test_cases.expected: The new customer appears in React
test_cases.actual: Created "Swagger User" directly through the API, then reloaded: listed in React: True
